prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a low-speed head-on collision claim. Injury: wrist fracture. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1091; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened following a low-speed head-on collision reported by the insured. Insured states the other vehicle crossed the centerline on a curve. Police report requested. Vehicle inspection assigned to the appraiser for the insured's car, with a repair estimate pending.

Entry 2: Claimant reports a wrist fracture sustained in the collision and has retained counsel. All further communication to be routed through the attorney's office. Requested medical authorization and prior treatment records. Reserve set for bodily injury pending review of medical documentation.

Entry 3: Received the police report. Officer noted minor front-end damage to both vehicles and no citations issued. Liability analysis indicates the other driver's centerline crossing is the probable cause, with comparative fault still under review. Reviewing photos from the scene.

Entry 4: Attorney's office sent a demand package including orthopedic records and imaging confirming a distal radius fracture. Treatment is ongoing and a surgical consult is noted. Requested itemized medical bills and wage loss documentation. Referred the file to the bodily injury unit for valuation.

Entry 5: Vehicle repair estimate reviewed and approved for payment to the repair facility. Rental coverage confirmed for the duration of repairs. Bodily injury claim remains open with medical bills and wage documentation outstanding. Follow-up with counsel scheduled to discuss next steps on settlement evaluation.
